The Abia State Government has dissolved the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club with immediate effect as the club battles to escape the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) relegation zone.
The decision, announced on Tuesday by the state government, follows a disappointing start to the 2026/27 season, which has left the two-time CAF Champions League winners 18th on the league table after 13 matches.
However, despite the planned wholesale changes, sources within the club claim that former Super Eagles captain Nwankwo Kanu may be allowed to continue as the club’s chairman.
In a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information, Okey Kanu, the government said it decided to address the club’s poor performance and identified administrative and structural challenges.
The statement said the government had concluded that far-reaching interventions were necessary to address the underlying problems affecting the club’s performance, administration and overall operations.
It consequently mandated the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development to lead the restructuring process, assess the club’s management framework and implement administrative, technical, operational and institutional reforms.
“The dissolution takes immediate effect,” the statement said.

All affected management and technical personnel, as well as individuals in possession of the club’s assets, properties, official documents and equipment, have been directed to hand them over to the ministry.
The ministry is expected to communicate further details about the handover arrangements and subsequent administrative procedures.
The latest setback came on Sunday when Enyimba suffered a 1-0 home defeat to Ikorodu City at the Enyimba Stadium in Aba. The result left them with three wins, two draws and eight defeats from 13 matches, giving them 11 points.
The latest intervention comes amid growing concerns about the club’s decline, which has continued despite changes in its technical and administrative structures.
In an April 2026 report , PREMIUM TIMES documented several problems affecting the club, including frequent coaching changes, questionable recruitment decisions, concerns over players’ welfare and administrative instability.
Enyimba went through four coaches in 29 league matches during the previous campaign, with Olarenwaju Yema, Stanley Eguma, Lawrence Ukaegbu and Emmanuel Deutsche taking charge at different periods.
The club also experienced changes in its sporting director position, while concerns were raised about delayed salaries, unpaid bonuses and inadequate support for injured players.
These challenges have contributed to the decline of a club that once set the standard for Nigerian football.
Enyimba’s most recent league title came in the 2023/24 season under former Super Eagles coach Finidi George. They have also won the CAF Champions League twice, in 2003 and 2004, establishing themselves as one of Africa’s most successful clubs.
The Abia State Government acknowledged the club’s historic contribution to Nigerian and African football, describing it as an important part of the state’s sporting heritage.
It assured supporters, players and the wider football community that the restructuring was intended to strengthen the club’s institutional capacity, restore accountability and return it to the competitive standards associated with its name.
For Enyimba, however, the immediate challenge remains escaping the relegation zone and restoring stability to a club whose recent struggles have raised questions about its ability to reclaim its former status.
